claim: Nr2f1a mutant zebrafish develop smaller atria due to reduced AC differentiation at the venous pole
source: Nr2f1a mutant zebrafish develop smaller atria due to reduced AC differentiation at the venous pole and fail to restrict the size of the AVC, which results in an expansion of AVC markers into the atrium (Duong et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Duong et al., 2018)

claim: Nr2f1a mutant zebrafish fail to restrict the size of the AVC, resulting in expansion of AVC markers into the atrium
source: Nr2f1a mutant zebrafish develop smaller atria due to reduced AC differentiation at the venous pole and fail to restrict the size of the AVC, which results in an expansion of AVC markers into the atrium (Duong et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Duong et al., 2018)

claim: RNA-seq of flow-sorted atrial cardiomyocytes from nr2f1a mutant zebrafish embryos showed 2077 upregulated and 1297 downregulated genes with >2-fold change relative to WT
source: The resulting RNA-seq dataset revealed 2077 upregulated and 1297 downregulated genes with >2-fold change in the nr2f1a mutant amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes relative to WT (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript

claim: Genes associated with AC differentiation, such as amhc, were decreased in amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes from nr2f1a mutant embryos relative to WT
source: Genes associated with AC differentiation, such as amhc itself, were decreased in the amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes captured from nr2f1a mutant embryos relative to the WT embryos, confirming the success of this approach (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B

claim: Nr2f1a mutant amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes show increased expression of genes associated with VC and outflow tract identity, such as irx4 and isl2 paralogs
source: However, we also observed two additional trends in the nr2f1a mutant amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes: an increase in the expression of genes associated with VC and outflow tract identity of the heart, such as the irx4 and isl2 paralogs (Bruneau et al., 2000; Bruneau et al., 2001; Targoff et al., 2013; Witzel et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citations to prior work on these genes

claim: Nr2f1a mutant amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes show misexpression of core genes associated with PC differentiation, with genes promoting PC differentiation (tbx3a and shox) being increased
source: and misexpression of core genes associated with PC differentiation, with genes shown to promote PC differentiation, such as tbx3a and shox, being increased (Hoogaars et al., 2007; Kenyon et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2011; Ribeiro et al., 2007; Sawada et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citations to prior work on these genes

claim: nkx2.5, a critical repressor of PC differentiation, was decreased in nr2f1a mutant amhc:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes
source: while nkx2.5, a critical repressor of PC differentiation, was decreased (Colombo et al., 2018; Espinoza-Lewis et al., 2011; Nakashima et al., 2014; Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B and citations to prior work on nkx2.5 function

claim: At 30 hpf, there is significant overlap of Amhc and Vmhc in heart tubes that is indistinguishable between WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: Although we found a significant overlap of Amhc and Vmhc in the heart tubes at 30 hpf, which was indistinguishable between WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–A", E–E")
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The number of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes (AVC) becomes significantly restricted by 48 hpf in WT embryo hearts
source: the number of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes, which we classify as cardiomyocytes of the AVC, becomes significantly restricted by 48 hpf in the hearts of WT embryos (Figure 1C and J–L; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–B").
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 1

claim: From 48 to 96 hpf, there remains a relatively constant and small number of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes in WT embryo hearts
source: Subsequently, from 48 to 96 hpf there remained a relatively constant and small number of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes in the hearts of WT embryos (Figure 1C, E, G and J–L; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D"; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 1 and supplements

claim: By 48 hpf, nr2f1a mutant hearts have a significant number of cardiomyocytes co-expressing Amhc and Vmhc
source: However, by 48 hpf in nr2f1a mutant hearts, there were still a significant number of cardiomyocytes co-expressing Amhc and Vmhc (Figure 1D and J–L; Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–F''; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 1 and supplements

claim: The number of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes within nr2f1a mutant hearts progressively reduces from 48 to 96 hpf
source: Interestingly, the number of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes within this region of nr2f1a mutant hearts was progressively reduced through 96 hpf (Figure 1F, H and J–L; Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–G", H-H"; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 1 and supplements

claim: There is a modest increase of Amhc+/Vmhc- cardiomyocytes in the atria of WT hearts from 48 to 96 hpf
source: While Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes remained constant over these stages, there was a modest increase of Amhc+/Vmhc- cardiomyocytes in the atria of WT hearts.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data from Figure 1

claim: Total Amhc+ cardiomyocytes diminish from 48 to 96 hpf in nr2f1a mutant hearts, primarily due to decrease in Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes
source: However, total Amhc+ cardiomyocytes (Amhc+/Vmhc- and Amhc+/Vmhc+) were found to diminish from 48 to 96 hpf in the nr2f1a mutant hearts, which was primarily due to the decrease in Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes as the number of Amhc+/Vmhc- cardiomyocytes, while dramatically reduced compared to WT hearts, did not change significantly over these stages (Figure 1J; Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H" and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1 and supplements

claim: There are more total Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant hearts compared to WT hearts across all timepoints from 48 to 96 hpf
source: Conversely, there were more total Vmhc+ (Amhc-/Vmhc+ and Amhc+/Vmhc+) cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant hearts compared to WT hearts across all timepoints, which primarily reflects the expansion of Vmhc expression within the enlarged AVC of the nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 1K; Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H" and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1 and supplements

claim: The number of Vmhc+-only (Amhc-/Vmhc+) cardiomyocytes progressively increases from 48 to 96 hpf in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: Furthermore, the number of Vmhc+-only (Amhc-/Vmhc+) cardiomyocytes progressively increased from 48 to 96 hpf in nr2f1a mutant hearts, complementing the loss of Amhc+/Vmhc+ cardiomyocytes within the AVC (Figure 1K; Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H" and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1 and supplements

claim: The total number of cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant hearts remains constant from 48 to 96 hpf
source: Interestingly, the total number of cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant hearts remained constant from 48 to 96 hpf, stages that showed a progressive increase in the total number of cardiomyocytes in WT hearts (Figure 1L)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1L

claim: WT hearts show a progressive increase in total number of cardiomyocytes from 48 to 96 hpf
source: Interestingly, the total number of cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant hearts remained constant from 48 to 96 hpf, stages that showed a progressive increase in the total number of cardiomyocytes in WT hearts (Figure 1L)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1L

claim: Cell death, as assayed with IHC for active Caspase 3, is not affected in nr2f1a mutant hearts from 72 to 96 hpf
source: Cell death, as assayed with IHC for active Caspase 3, and proliferation, as assayed with IHC for phosphohistone H3 (pHH3), were not affected at these stages in nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–D; Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: Proliferation, as assayed with IHC for phosphohistone H3 (pHH3), is not affected in nr2f1a mutant hearts from 48 to 96 hpf
source: Cell death, as assayed with IHC for active Caspase 3, and proliferation, as assayed with IHC for phosphohistone H3 (pHH3), were not affected at these stages in nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–D; Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–F

claim: EdU pulses at 48 or 72 hpf show that Amhc+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant hearts do not have reduced proliferation
source: Similarly, EdU pulses at 48 or 72 hpf showed that Amhc+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutants hearts also do not have reduced proliferation (Figure 1—figure supplement 4G–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU proliferation assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4G–M

claim: Amhc- cardiomyocytes (predominantly VCs) show reduced proliferation in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: However, Amhc- cardiomyocytes, which are predominantly VCs, did show reduced proliferation (Figure 1—figure supplement 4G–M)
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU proliferation assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4G–M

claim: The lack of increase in heart size in nr2f1a mutants primarily reflects a lack of ventricular growth
source: suggesting the lack of increase in heart size in nr2f1a mutants primarily reflects a lack of ventricular growth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the proliferation data showing reduced proliferation in Amhc- (ventricular) cardiomyocytes

claim: Changes in different cardiomyocyte populations of nr2f1a mutant hearts are not due to increased cell death or proliferation
source: Thus, our data indicate that changes in the different cardiomyocyte populations of nr2f1a mutants hearts are not due to increased cell death or proliferation.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cell death and proliferation assay data

claim: The expansion and acquisition of VC identity within nr2f1a mutant hearts is regionally restricted to cardiomyocytes comprising the expanded AVC
source: Collectively, these results show that the expansion and acquisition of VC identity within nr2f1a mutant hearts is regionally restricted, with cardiomyocytes comprising the expanded AVC that initially expresses both AC and VC differentiation markers resolving to VC identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the IHC and quantification data showing progressive changes in marker expression

claim: Cardiomyocytes comprising the expanded AVC in nr2f1a mutants initially express both AC and VC differentiation markers and resolve to VC identity
source: Collectively, these results show that the expansion and acquisition of VC identity within nr2f1a mutant hearts is regionally restricted, with cardiomyocytes comprising the expanded AVC that initially expresses both AC and VC differentiation markers resolving to VC identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the IHC and quantification data showing progressive changes in marker expression

claim: At 48 hpf, there is no overt difference in Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression between WT and nr2f1a mutant embryos
source: At 48 hpf, we found no overt difference in Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression between the WT and nr2f1a mutant embryos (Figure 2A and B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–A''', D–D''')
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 2A and B

claim: There is a progressive expansion of Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression from the venous pole throughout Amhc+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant atria through 96 hpf
source: However, while Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression is normally restricted to the venous pole in WT hearts, we found a progressive expansion of Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression from the venous pole throughout the Amhc+ cardiomyocytes in the atrium of the nr2f1a mutant hearts through 96 hpf (Figure 2C–F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C''', E–F''').
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 2C–F and supplements

claim: There is a concurrent increase in fgf13a:EGFP+/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes and decrease in fgf13a:EGFP-/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes within nr2f1a mutant atria
source: Quantification of Amhc+ cardiomyocytes co-expressing the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) transgene via incorporation of the Tg(myl7:DsRed2-NLS) transgene confirmed the concurrent increase in fgf13a:EGFP+/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes and decrease in fgf13a:EGFP-/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes within the nr2f1a mutant atria (Figure 2G and H)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2G and H

claim: RT-qPCR on flow-sorted cardiomyocytes from 96 hpf embryos shows an increase in PC differentiation marker expression in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: Additionally, real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) on flow-sorted cardiomyocytes from 96 hpf embryos using the pan-cardiac Tg(myl7:EGFP) transgene (Huang et al., 2003) showed an increase in PC differentiation marker expression, as well as vmhc expression, and decrease in amhc at these stages in nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 2J and K)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2K

claim: RT-qPCR on flow-sorted cardiomyocytes from 96 hpf embryos shows an increase in vmhc expression in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: Additionally, real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) on flow-sorted cardiomyocytes from 96 hpf embryos using the pan-cardiac Tg(myl7:EGFP) transgene (Huang et al., 2003) showed an increase in PC differentiation marker expression, as well as vmhc expression, and decrease in amhc at these stages in nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 2J and K)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2K

claim: RT-qPCR on flow-sorted cardiomyocytes from 96 hpf embryos shows a decrease in amhc expression in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: Additionally, real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) on flow-sorted cardiomyocytes from 96 hpf embryos using the pan-cardiac Tg(myl7:EGFP) transgene (Huang et al., 2003) showed an increase in PC differentiation marker expression, as well as vmhc expression, and decrease in amhc at these stages in nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 2J and K)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2K

claim: All fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes within the atria of both WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts at 96 hpf co-express both photoconverted (red) NLS-KikGR and newly expressed (green) NLS-KikGR
source: We found that in both WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts all fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes within the atria co-expressed both photoconverted (red) NLS-KikGR and newly expressed (green) NLS-KikGR, including those in the expanded fgf13a:EGFP+ expression domain and venous pole of nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–E").
evidence: This claim is supported by photoconversion lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: The absence of green-only, newly differentiated NLS-KikGR+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant atria at 96 hpf indicates that all fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes were present in the atrium at 72 hpf
source: The absence of green-only, newly differentiated NLS-KikGR+ cardiomyocytes in the nr2f1a mutant atria at 96 hpf indicates that all of the fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes were present in the atrium at 72 hpf.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the photoconversion lineage tracing data

claim: Venous Amhc+ ACs are progressively transdifferentiating into PCs in the absence of Nr2f1a
source: Thus, our data support that venous Amhc+ ACs are progressively transdifferentiating into PCs in the absence of Nr2f1a.
evidence: This claim is supported by the lineage tracing and marker expression data

claim: At 48 hpf, there is no difference in heart rate between WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: At 48 hpf, there was no difference in heart rate between WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by heart rate analysis data shown in Figure 3C

claim: As the heart rate of WT embryos increases through 96 hpf, the heart rate of nr2f1a mutant hearts fails to increase
source: However, as the heart rate of WT embryos increased through 96 hpf, the heart rate of nr2f1a mutant hearts failed to increase (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by heart rate analysis data shown in Figure 3C

claim: The intrinsic bradycardia in nr2f1a mutants is related to effects on the duration and extent of repolarization with evidence of modest hyperpolarization in both heterozygous and homozygous nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: The intrinsic bradycardia we observed appeared to be related to effects on the duration and extent of repolarization with evidence of modest hyperpolarization in both heterozygous and homozygous nr2f1a mutant hearts, as well as substantial prolongation of repolarization in the homozygous nr2f1a mutant hearts, as conservatively assessed based on the action potential duration at 20% repolarization (APD20) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical voltage mapping data shown in Figure 3D

claim: There is substantial prolongation of repolarization in homozygous nr2f1a mutant hearts, as assessed by APD20
source: The intrinsic bradycardia we observed appeared to be related to effects on the duration and extent of repolarization with evidence of modest hyperpolarization in both heterozygous and homozygous nr2f1a mutant hearts, as well as substantial prolongation of repolarization in the homozygous nr2f1a mutant hearts, as conservatively assessed based on the action potential duration at 20% repolarization (APD20) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical voltage mapping data shown in Figure 3D

claim: At 48 hpf, ACs in nr2f1a mutant hearts depolarize more slowly compared to WT and heterozygous nr2f1a atria
source: Measuring the APD20 within the center of the atria (Figure 3A), which acquires PC marker expression in the nr2f1a mutants based on the IHC analysis, showed that even at 48 hpf the ACs in nr2f1a mutant hearts depolarize more slowly compared to WT and heterozygous nr2f1a atria (Figure 3E; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by APD20 measurements shown in Figure 3E

claim: There is significantly slower conduction across nr2f1a mutant atria by 96 hpf
source: There was evidence of significantly slower conduction across the nr2f1a mutant atria by 96 hpf (Figure 3F–L; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), but with no effect on Vmax (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This claim is supported by conduction velocity measurements shown in Figure 3F–L

claim: There is no effect on Vmax in nr2f1a mutant atria
source: There was evidence of significantly slower conduction across the nr2f1a mutant atria by 96 hpf (Figure 3F–L; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), but with no effect on Vmax (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This claim is supported by Vmax measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C

claim: There is no evidence of the emergence of the AVC slow conduction zone in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: Remarkably, there was no evidence of the emergence of the AVC slow conduction zone in the nr2f1a mutant hearts that is characteristic of the AV junction and the resultant sequential chamber contraction that is the hallmark of the vertebrate heart (Figure 3G–L)
evidence: This claim is supported by isochronal maps shown in Figure 3G–L

claim: More venous ACs in nr2f1a mutant hearts are adopting a functional identity that exhibits delayed repolarization and reduced intercellular coupling, closer to the physiology of cardiomyocytes of the central conduction system
source: Collectively, our data support that more venous ACs in nr2f1a mutant hearts are adopting a functional identity that exhibits delayed repolarization and reduced intercellular coupling, closer to the physiology of the cardiomyocytes of the central conduction system and paralleling the PC-associated gene expression changes we observe within the nr2f1a mutant atria.
evidence: This claim is supported by the electrophysiological data and gene expression data

claim: In WT hearts at 48 through 96 hpf, Nkx2.5 is expressed throughout the atrial myocardium but is predominantly excluded from PCs at the venous pole
source: IHC for Nkx2.5 and either the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) reporter or Isl1 both showed that in WT hearts at 48 through 96 hpf Nkx2.5 is expressed throughout the atrial myocardium but is predominantly excluded from the PCs at the venous pole (Figure 4A–C"; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), consistent with what has been reported in zebrafish and mice (Colombo et al., 2018; Mommersteeg et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 4 and citations to prior work

claim: At 48 hpf in nr2f1a mutants, Nkx2.5 shows a similar complementary pattern with the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) reporter despite the smaller atria
source: At 48 hpf in nr2f1a mutants, Nkx2.5 shows a similar complementary pattern with the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) reporter despite the smaller atria (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 4D

claim: As the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) reporter expands toward the AVC into Amhc+ ACs through 96 hpf in nr2f1a mutants, Nkx2.5 expression recedes from the venous pole and predominantly maintains the complementary expression pattern
source: As the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) reporter expands toward the AVC into the Amhc+ ACs through 96 hpf in nr2f1a mutants, Nkx2.5 expression recedes from the venous pole and predominantly maintains the complementary expression pattern (Figure 4E–F").
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 4E–F"

claim: A progressive loss of Nkx2.5 within ACs correlates with and abuts the expansion of PC identity in nr2f1a mutant atria
source: Thus, a progressive loss of Nkx2.5 within ACs correlates with and abuts the expansion of PC identity in nr2f1a mutant atria.
evidence: This claim is supported by the IHC data showing complementary patterns of Nkx2.5 and PC markers

claim: At 48 hpf, there is a modest decrease in the number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes in Nkx2.5-EGFP+ WT hearts compared to Nkx2.5-EGFP- WT siblings
source: At 48 hpf, there was a modest decrease in the number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes in Nkx2.5-EGFP+ WT hearts compared to the Nkx2.5-EGFP- WT siblings (Figure 5B, C, J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data from heat-shock experiments shown in Figure 5

claim: Nkx2.5-EGFP+ nr2f1a mutants have a complete absence of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes at the venous pole at 48 hpf
source: However, Nkx2.5-EGFP+ nr2f1a mutants had a complete absence of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes at the venous pole (Figure 5F, G, J and K)
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data from heat-shock experiments shown in Figure 5

claim: Nkx2.5 is sufficient to repress PC differentiation in nr2f1a mutant hearts
source: suggesting that Nkx2.5 is sufficient to repress PC differentiation in nr2f1a mutant hearts and, further, that nr2f1a mutant ACs may be sensitized to increased Nkx2.5 expression.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the heat-shock rescue experiments showing loss of PC markers with Nkx2.5 overexpression

claim: nr2f1a mutant ACs may be sensitized to increased Nkx2.5 expression
source: suggesting that Nkx2.5 is sufficient to repress PC differentiation in nr2f1a mutant hearts and, further, that nr2f1a mutant ACs may be sensitized to increased Nkx2.5 expression.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the complete absence of PC markers in nr2f1a mutants with Nkx2.5 overexpression

claim: At 96 hpf, both Nkx2.5-EGFP+ WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts have an increased number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes compared to those at 48 hpf
source: At 96 hpf, both Nkx2.5-EGFP+ WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts had an increased number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes compared to those at 48 hpf, yet Nkx2.5-EGFP+ nr2f1a mutants still had significantly fewer fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes than mutants lacking the transgene (Figure 5D, E and H–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data from heat-shock experiments shown in Figure 5

claim: Nkx2.5-EGFP+ nr2f1a mutants at 96 hpf have significantly fewer fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes than mutants lacking the transgene
source: At 96 hpf, both Nkx2.5-EGFP+ WT and nr2f1a mutant hearts had an increased number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes compared to those at 48 hpf, yet Nkx2.5-EGFP+ nr2f1a mutants still had significantly fewer fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes than mutants lacking the transgene (Figure 5D, E and H–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data from heat-shock experiments shown in Figure 5

claim: Overexpression of Nkx2.5 does not rescue the heart rate of nr2f1a mutants at 96 hpf
source: While we see a repression of the fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocyte expansion at 48 hpf, we found that the overexpression of Nkx2.5 did not rescue the heart rate of nr2f1a mutants at 96 hpf when we observe the resumption of the PC reporter (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by heart rate data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: Additional Nkx2.5-independent mechanisms downstream of Nr2f1a also contribute to the inhibition of PC identity
source: suggesting that despite the inhibition of the reporter expansion, additional Nkx2.5-independent mechanisms downstream of Nr2f1a also contribute to the inhibition of PC identity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the incomplete rescue of heart rate despite repression of PC marker expansion

claim: Heat-shock induction of Nkx2.5-EGFP at 40 hpf can repress the expansion of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant atria
source: We found that heat-shock induction of Nkx2.5-EGFP at 40 hpf could also repress the expansion of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes in nr2f1a mutant atria (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C, F, G, J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by heat-shock experiment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: The repression of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes within mutant atria is not as effective or prolonged with heat-shock induction of Nkx2.5-EGFP at 40 hpf compared to 20 hpf
source: However, the repression of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes within the mutant atria was not as effective or prolonged as the heat-shock induction of Nkx2.5-EGFP at 20 hpf (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D, E and H–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of heat-shock experiment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: Nr2f1a prevents the expansion of PC identity within the venous pole of the atrium at least in part through promoting or maintaining Nkx2.5 in ACs
source: Overall, these data suggest that Nr2f1a prevents the expansion of PC identity within the venous pole of the atrium at least in part through promoting or maintaining Nkx2.5 in ACs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the genetic epistasis experiments showing Nkx2.5 can repress PC marker expansion

claim: A putative enhancer region ~55 kb upstream of the nkx2.5 transcriptional start site closes in nr2f1a mutant atria and contains an Nr2f binding site
source: One of the peaks that was revealed to close in nr2f1a mutant atria and contain an Nr2f binding site was ~55 kb upstream of the nkx2.5 transcriptional start site (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 6A

claim: The putative nkx2.5 enhancer is expressed in a group of cardiomyocytes at the venous pole of the atrium
source: Remarkably, stable transgenic lines showed that this putative enhancer is expressed in a group of cardiomyocytes at the venous pole of the atrium (Figure 6C)
evidence: This claim is supported by transgenic reporter data shown in Figure 6C

claim: The Tg(–55nkx2.5:EGFP) transgene is expressed in ACs directly adjacent to Isl1+ PCs
source: which are directly adjacent to Isl1+ PCs (Figure 6D and D').
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 6D and D'

claim: The number of atria with Tg(–55nkx2.5:EGFP) expression is significantly decreased in nr2f1a mutants compared to WT
source: We found the number of atria with Tg(–55nkx2.5:EGFP) expression was significantly decreased in nr2f1a mutants compared to WT, suggesting that Nr2f1a is required for enhancer expression or for those cardiomyocytes to develop (Figure 6C, E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of transgenic reporter expression shown in Figure 6F

claim: Nr2f1a is required for the –55nkx2.5 enhancer expression or for those cardiomyocytes to develop
source: We found the number of atria with Tg(–55nkx2.5:EGFP) expression was significantly decreased in nr2f1a mutants compared to WT, suggesting that Nr2f1a is required for enhancer expression or for those cardiomyocytes to develop (Figure 6C, E and F).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the loss of enhancer expression in nr2f1a mutants

claim: –55nkx2.5 crispant embryos have reduced Nkx2.5 expression that does not extend as far toward the venous pole of their atria compared to control embryos
source: IHC for Nkx2.5 in –55nkx2.5 crispants showed that Nkx2.5 did not extend as far toward to the venous pole of their atria and that they had a significant reduction in the number of Nkx2.5+/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes within the atria compared to control embryos (Figure 6G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 6G–I

claim: –55nkx2.5 crispant embryos have a significant reduction in the number of Nkx2.5+/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes within the atria compared to control embryos
source: IHC for Nkx2.5 in –55nkx2.5 crispants showed that Nkx2.5 did not extend as far toward to the venous pole of their atria and that they had a significant reduction in the number of Nkx2.5+/Amhc+ cardiomyocytes within the atria compared to control embryos (Figure 6G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 6G–I

claim: –55nkx2.5 crispant embryos carrying the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) and Tg(myl7:DsRed2-NLS) transgenes show an arterial-directed expansion of Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression within their atria
source: Conversely, –55nkx2.5 crispant embryos concurrently carrying the Et(fgf13a:EGFP) and Tg(myl7:DsRed2-NLS) transgenes showed an arterial-directed expansion of Et(fgf13a:EGFP) expression within their atria and an increase in the number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes at the venous pole compared to control embryos (Figure 6J–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and quantification data shown in Figure 6J–L

claim: –55nkx2.5 crispant embryos have an increase in the number of fgf13a:EGFP+ cardiomyocytes at the venous pole compared to control embryos
